headline: 32 arrested over Awami League procession in Gulshan
summary: Dhaka Metropolitan Police arrested leaders and activists of the banned party and its associate bodies for participating in a procession in the capital.
details: Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) have arrested 32 leaders and activists of the Awami League and its associate bodies for allegedly taking part in a procession in the capital's Gulshan area yesterday.

DMP Additional Deputy Commissioner (Media) Niaz Mehedi confirmed the arrests, while Deputy Commissioner (Media) Akter Hossain stated that the arrests were made in a case filed with Gulshan Police Station under the Anti-Terrorism Act.
Gulshan Police Station Inspector (Investigation) Mokhlesur Rahman told The Daily Star that a case has been filed over the procession.

The government banned all activities of the Awami League and its affiliated organisations on May 11 last year, citing allegations of killings, genocide, and crimes against humanity during the July uprising.

headline_marked: Govt to [[align Bangla and English-medium curricula]] for common standards
headline: Govt to align Bangla and English-medium curricula for common standards
summary: State Minister Bobby Hajjaj says the government will establish minimum standards for basic knowledge and skills across all educational streams.
details: The government will take steps to align Bangla- and English-medium curricula to ensure a common minimum standard of basic knowledge and skills for all students, State Minister for Primary and Mass Education Bobby Hajjaj announced.

Speaking at the School Leaders Conference 2026 in Dhaka, the Minister stated that while differences between institutions may exist, there should not be major disparities in the basic standard of education regardless of the stream.
The government plans to implement coordinated initiatives across four key areas: curriculum, infrastructure, teacher training, and technology to create a level playing field for all students.

Bobby Hajjaj emphasized that no teacher should be assigned to a classroom without proper training and called for quick reforms in primary education, including clear standards for classroom size and learning hours.
The government also intends to learn from the experience of English-medium schools, particularly their use of Learning Management Systems (LMS), to improve the overall education system.
Regarding the new curriculum, the Minister assured that the government would consult with relevant stakeholders and incorporate their experiences and opinions into the formulation process.
caption:
No more major disparities in education. The government is moving to align Bangla and English-medium curricula.

The government will take steps to align Bangla- and English-medium curricula to ensure a common minimum standard of basic knowledge and skills for all students, State Minister for Primary and Mass Education Bobby Hajjaj announced.

Speaking at the School Leaders Conference 2026 in Dhaka, the Minister stated that while differences between institutions may exist, there should not be major disparities in the basic standard of education regardless of the stream.

The government plans to implement coordinated initiatives across four key areas: curriculum, infrastructure, teacher training, and technology to create a level playing field for all students.

Bobby Hajjaj emphasized that no teacher should be assigned to a classroom without proper training and called for quick reforms in primary education, including clear standards for classroom size and learning hours.

The government also intends to learn from the experience of English-medium schools, particularly their use of Learning Management Systems (LMS), to improve the overall education system.

Regarding the new curriculum, the Minister assured that the government would consult with relevant stakeholders and incorporate their experiences and opinions into the formulation process.
